P1.evidence: Two of the four frame parts: 'Where are you today, John? Where do you really want to be? Once we have crystal clear clarity as to those two things, I can present to you one of the many options that we have, okay?' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was a single 'Okay'. Open question ran verbatim: 'So I'll turn the leaf over to you, John. How can we potentially help you?' No read-back of Kim's setter notes despite this being a KFS-set call.

P2.evidence: Only the work question ran — 'What are you doing now?' produced real estate agent plus school bus driver and 'both jobs require a lot of sitting', which the rep used well later. Everything else was skipped. Age came from the prospect volunteering 'I'm 62'. Height and weight were never asked, despite the prospect flagging the subject himself with 'I hate to even tell people how much I weigh' — an open invitation the rep did not take. No health question at all, so a detached retina operated on seven weeks earlier surfaced only because the prospect mentioned it in passing. No injury question, so 'I really can't [jog] anymore, because it's so hard on my body' was never explored. No training week, no diet, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: Strong on the personal why: 'when you go about your day, you're seeing yourself in the mirror... what is the bit that pisses you off the most?' then the bridge 'how do you see yourself becoming better in these different areas of your life by being better physically?' and again 'giving you a higher chance of having the career that you want to have?' Reached identity via the mind-versus-body scale — he rated his mind a nine or ten and his body 'about a two'. But P3f never ran: nobody else was ever brought into the frame, which is a notable omission for a man who had just described three years caring for his mother until she died.

P4.evidence: The 'why not' sequence ran properly — 'you said part of the reason you're pissed off is that you're not doing anything about it... Why not, man?' produced 'laziness', and 'so when did that change?' unlocked the whole caregiving and job-loss history. Used the mentor frame 'what has kept you stuck in the past will keep you stuck in the future'. Weakened by leading the root cause rather than letting him name it — 'would you say the root cause of your laziness is being somewhat comfortable over the past few years?' was rejected outright with 'I don't know if it's so much comfortable'. Past training attempts were prospect-led, never asked for.

P5.evidence: Best consequence work in this batch so far, though built from different components than the script's. Ran the want-or-need frame ('would you say it's a want or a need for you to actually step into the higher self of you?' — 'It's a need'), then 'Why do you say it's a need?' which produced the cost of inaction in his own words: 'if I don't do something, I don't want to get stuck here.' Closed the phase with a genuine line in the sand — 'So John, are you actually ready to take that step?' / 'Yep. I'm ready to do it.' / 'I'll hold you accountable to it.' The two-year projection and the 'willing to settle' question were never asked.

P6.evidence: P6a ran close to verbatim: 'the most important question I have for you, John, is do you believe you're internally capable of following a step-by-step process and being a good student of Trevor to make this happen?' — 'Yes, I am.' The 1-10 check also produced a clear signal ('I, I need it. I need that. I need it.') and the rep followed it with 'what pieces gives you the confidence?' before moving on, so P6c was respected. P6b — 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' — never ran, and that is the question that would have surfaced the money problem before the price rather than after it.

P11.evidence: Payment was declined at the first ask and the downsell was declined too, so no onboarding, agreement or welcome-email step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest money trigger in the batch and not one scripted move ran. No isolate ('finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up', no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The rep's entire response was 'Well, good. I appreciate that. I appreciate you just being upfront' followed by a product change. In fairness the prospect had pre-empted the payment plan himself ('not even on a payment plan'), but the script asks the rep to verify that rather than accept it.

Run pre-emptively rather than in response to a stall, which is the notable thing here. The rep set up the plane move himself — 'imagine yourself on a 40-foot plane, you're about to jump off, skydive, what emotion, feeling, would rise in yourself?' — got 'Fear', pushed into where fear had cost him before ('the market crashed on me... I just went into a spiral'), then landed the responsibility question: 'who's actually responsible for making that step outside of their comfort zone, despite the fear?' Answer: 'It's only me.' That converted directly into the readiness commitment. Good process regardless of outcome.

Script gap: this prospect had genuinely zero liquidity — two months without income following eye surgery, no savings mentioned, unable to fund even a $200/mo product. OC is built for latent capacity, not absent capacity, and there is no scripted path for a prospect who cannot pay at any tier. The real failure sits upstream of the play: he disclosed 'I don't know how I'm going to make ends meet' at 00:05:33 and nobody, setter or closer, qualified on it before twenty minutes of pitch.

notes: Genuinely the rep's strongest emotional work in this batch — the fear frame, the responsibility question and the want-versus-need sequence all ran and all landed — spent on a prospect who had told him in minute five that he had not worked in two months after eye surgery. Two coaching points, in order: qualify on money before the pillars when hard financial distress is disclosed, and ask the health questions. A man seven weeks out from retinal surgery had his medical history skipped entirely.
